items.title: Amex introduces a framework to prevent AI agents from making unauthorized purchases
items.summary: American Express is introducing a new framework designed to ensure AI agents only make purchases their users have authorized, potentially preventing costly mistakes and disputes as AI-powered shopping grows.

items.title: Just 5 years in, interactive chatbot platform Character.AI files for bankruptcy
items.summary: The startup will sell some of its assets to Disney for $20 million.

items.title: Meta releases its first frontier model, Muse Wonder
items.summary: Where Muse Spark aimed to be a lightweight model that could perform at low latency, the Wonder models are larger and said to be more capable, with higher benchmark scores and better results on complex tasks like coding.

items.title: WindBorne wins a hefty US Air Force contract for its balloon data
items.summary: A Silicon Valley startup that uses weather balloons and AI to predict the weather won a U.S. military contract worth almost $50 million.

items.title: Honeyjar offers AI tools to improve PR and comms at every company
items.summary: Journalists, entrepreneurs, and even some public relations professionals will tell you that the PR process is broken. But could AI actually make things better?

items.title: Microsoft president says UK is best placed to drive AI regulation
items.summary: Microsoft president Brad Smith calls for urgent AI regulation, saying milk and washing machines have more oversight than AI companies.

items.title: This AI startup says it can generate permit-ready blueprints in minutes
items.summary: Blueprints AI, a bootstrapped startup based in Santa Monica, developed software that produces code-compliant construction blueprints from a photo, PDF, or sketch.

items.title: Former Plaud exec raises $26M for AI app that listens to you in the background
items.summary: One of the core promises of AI is that the more it knows about a person, the better it will be able to assist them with tasks and make appropriate suggestions, which, if you'll believe the tech companies, requires apps and devices to listen, watch, or record users' activity all the time and gather all possible context.
